question: GQ-001
subject: the served page searched titles; the CLI searched 3.1 million passages

the_gap.library.html: a 10.5 MB STATIC file searching titles and chapter headings only
the_gap.the_cli: 3,135,554 passages across the printed and modern-spelling indexes
the_gap.meaning: a reader on the web got a fundamentally weaker search than one at a terminal — the same "capability exists, nothing surfaces it" defect the search CLI itself was written to fix, one layer up

why_it_was_cheap: a server already runs — com.siso.librarian-observatory, 32 lines, serving public/ on 8765. Adding /search is an endpoint, not infrastructure.
delegates_rather_than_duplicates: the endpoint shells out to search-library.mjs instead of copying its SQL. That exclusion logic took four failed attempts to get right (rowid join, per-term LIKE, candidate cap); a second copy would drift silently.

a_defect_the_adversarial_test_found.the_database_was_never_at_risk: the connection is mode=ro and FTS5 rejected the string as invalid grammar; book_ext still holds 2,124 rows
a_defect_the_adversarial_test_found.but: the CLI died with a Node stack trace instead of saying what was wrong
a_defect_the_adversarial_test_found.fix: a malformed query now exits 65 (EX_DATAERR) with the FTS5 reason and a syntax hint; the endpoint maps that to HTTP 400, distinct from 500 (failure) and 504 (timeout)

a_false_alarm_i_chased: a 500 that should have been 400 was a STALE server process, not a code defect — confirmed by inspecting err.status directly (65, as designed) before changing anything
